government.note: Parliamentary republic with a unicameral National Assembly of 240 members. The directly elected President (two-round system, five-year term, at most two terms) is chiefly an arbiter between institutions and is not part of the executive; when the Assembly cannot form a government the President appoints a caretaker Prime Minister and calls an election, which happened repeatedly from 2013 and during the 2021-2026 political crisis (seven snap elections from April 2021 to April 2026). A Vice President, elected on the same ticket, completes the term if the President resigns: Iliana Iotova succeeded Rumen Radev on 23 January 2026, and Radev became Prime Minister after his new coalition won the April 2026 election.

system.note: Open-list PR in 31 multi-member constituencies (4 to 19 seats), 4% national threshold for parties and coalitions, seats by largest remainder with a Hare quota (as described for 2026). The 2009 election used a mixed system with 31 single-member seats. seats_2000 is the result of the April 1997 election: United Democratic Forces (ODS) 137 recorded under the SDS, Democratic Left 58 under the BSP, Union for National Salvation 19 under the DPS. Mid-term changes before 1 January 2000 were not checked.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from the April 1997 National Assembly vote (shares computed from the vote counts): United Democratic Forces 52.26% (SDS-led centre-right alliance, recorded as liberal conservative), Democratic Left (BSP-led) 22.07% and Bulgarian Euro-Left 5.50% (social democrat), Union for National Salvation (DPS-led) 7.60% (regionalist: the DPS represents mainly the Turkish minority), Bulgarian Business Bloc 4.93% (populist, recorded as right_populist), Communist Party of Bulgaria 1.20%, Alliance for the Tsar 1.10% (constitutional monarchist), other lists and independents 5.34% (big_tent).
